title: The binary-mess construction does not ensure satisfaction of each formula.
details: 2011-11-17 edition, Theorem5.15 implication(c) to(d), printed p.133 (PDF149). The proposed B_Sigma consists of restrictions of chosen realizations of arbitrary finite fragments. Take Sigma={p, p or not-p}. A realization of the tautology-only fragment may give p=0, while fragments containing p give p=1. The resulting binary mess permits both values on the one-variable domain, so a total function consistent with it can refute p. The assertion that every such consistent function realizes Sigma is false. In addition, choosing one realization for each fragment is unavailable in a ZF-only proof without further justification. Repair: bypass this step. On X=all total Boolean valuations, the sets of valuations satisfying each formula have the finite intersection property. Extend their generated proper filter using the ultrafilter theorem. Define each atom truth value from its coordinate truth set; structural induction using ultrafilter Boolean laws proves the resulting valuation satisfies Sigma. In the preceding(b) to(c) argument, intersect the coordinate agreement sets with the already-present A_P to justify membership in the binary mess.
